title: Throw a blob to a target by backprop
objective: Make the forward MLS-MPM blob differentiable and solve an inverse-control task end to end: find a single shared initial velocity v0 so the blob's center of mass lands on the target (0.7, 0.35) after 512 simulation steps, purely by backpropagating through the simulation.
findings: Backprop through the full 512-step rollout yields usable gradients. Adam drove the loss from 0.144 to 1.8e-4 in 68 iterations and the blob lands on the target, which proves the rollout is genuinely differentiable from end to end. The same run exposed the project's first real pathology, a NaN gradient at long horizon, which became its own direction (Long-rollout gradient pathologies).
